// products root is a MOUNT POINT (produ: product_root and every canonical_artifacts path stay LOGICAL — they always start with products/, whatever disk the trees are actually on. Resolve with .agent/scripts/resolve-products-root.mjs; never store an absolute path in a logical field, or this manifest stops being readable on another machine.

products_root_abs / product_root_abs are DERIVED, per-machine mirrors, refreshed by whichever command touches the manifest. They exist so slim-context agents (Developer 08, which never reads product-workspace.md) get absolute paths and resolve nothing. Never trust a stale value carried over from another machine — rewrite it and continue.
// two-level identity (schema 8+, when t: For content-sdk head-app runs (product-workspace.md § 1b-i / § 3): product_slug + product_root point at the HEAD APP — the pipeline-run workspace where project-planning/ lives, e.g. products/head-application/<project-slug>/<head-app-slug>.

The four fields above name the Deploy PROJECT (= one CM server) the head app belongs to: deploy_project_name = the verbatim Deploy project name (spaces/caps allowed, e.g. 'CHAH DevEx Journey'); project_slug = the space-free project folder; project_root = products/head-application/<project-slug>; cm_code_base = <project_root>/cm (NEW CM) or the operator's existing CM path (EXISTING CM, no cm/ created).
All head apps under one project share ONE cm_code_base + ONE Deploy project. Leave these null for marketplace / personal / legacy-flat products.
// repo_topology: How this run's deployables map onto git repos, when the platform pack offers a choice (`repo_topology.values` in pack.json). Content SDK offers two and BOTH are current: 'repo-per-deployable' (the head app is its own repo, a sibling of cm/) and 'monorepo' (ONE repo at cm/ holding authoring/ beside sites/<head-app-slug>/, with one root xmcloud.build.json). Asked in the /create-prd discovery grill, at intake, alongside the deploy-project + head-app names.

RECORD IT EVEN WHEN THE OPERATOR TOOK THE DEFAULT. Every downstream stage re-resolves its pack brief with `--topology <this value>` and gets `workspace` + `repo_setup` already resolved for it; an absent field re-defaults to repo-per-deployable, so a monorepo run would provision, ship and publish against the wrong paths while every one of those stages reported green.
Leave null when the platform declares a single fixed topology (marketplace) or none. Null means 'nothing to choose', not 'not asked yet'.
// packs: The resolved composition (platform-pack.md § 3). Written by M0 at intake. The nulls are recorded EXPLICITLY — "platform": "none" means resolved-and-the-answer-is-none, which an absent key cannot say. The slot was UNDECLARED until 2026-08-26 though step 18 and Validation both require it; runs worked only because manifest-write.mjs creates it on merge.

signals: new product — nothing to inherit (no prior manifest) and nothing to detect (no tree); M0 ladder rung 4. Resolved by /start-flow and carried into /create-prd step 0.

// workspace: Names resolved from an active platform pack's `workspace.naming` (ONE owner — pack.json, not the command). `brand_name` is the ROOT of the derive chain: deploy_project_name / project_slug / head_app_slug all descend from it, so an unresolved brand_name leaves every one of them null rather than guessed. Declared 2026-08-27 — until then packs resolved these and the template had nowhere to put them, so each run invented a path. Slots exist for every name a shipped pack lists under `workspace.naming.tenant_facing` — `site_name` / `editing_host_name` (content-sdk) and `app_name` (marketplace) were missing until 2026-08-28, so the field the `required_at` rule is NAMED after could not be recorded where the rule checks it, and one run repurposed `brand_name` for a Cloud Portal app name.
// variables: Pack-declared build variables (`variables` in pack.json) once resolved — e.g. the Content SDK router, the Marketplace auth mode. Free-form by design: the owning pack defines the keys, so core cannot enumerate them.
// work_item_type — schema 8 discriminat: work_item_type is the keystone discriminator set at intake by /create-prd (prd), /create-frd (frd), or /create-bug (bug). Every downstream command reads it to pick the weight-preset, the operator-gate count (prd=2, frd=1, bug=0+valves), and which stages to skip (bug skips architect+UI; frd skips architect+UI unless an ADR-worthy decision or UI scope exists).

SAME ARTIFACT SLOTS, DIFFERENT FILL. canonical_artifacts.prd / prd_minimal hold the SPEC and SPEC-MINIMAL regardless of type — for an FRD they point at frd-NNN.md / frd-minimal-NNN.md; for a bug at bug-NNN.md / bug-minimal-NNN.md. The slot names stay `prd` / `prd_minimal` so downstream read paths (esp. Developer-08's `prd_minimal + task_breakdown`) are unchanged. The misnomer is intentional and documented.
ID prefixes: PRD-NNN / FRD-NNN / BUG-NNN, per-product numbering namespaces. Branch names: prd-NNN / frd-NNN / bug-NNN.

PROMOTION is re-classify + enrich, never restart: when a bug's root cause is a design flaw (not-contained valve) or an FRD balloons, work_item_type flips upward and the intake doc is enriched in place (bug repro/expected become FRD problem/AC; the minimal block carries forward). Record a stage_history entry { stage: "promoted", outcome: "superseded", one_line: "BUG-003 promoted to FRD-004 — root cause is design, not a contained fix" }.
Legacy: schema-7-and-prior manifests have no work_item_type. Readers treat its absence as work_item_type: prd (the only type that existed).
// platform_target: RETIRED 2026-08-23 — superseded by packs{}. M0 no longer writes it. Ladder rung 2 (inherit-legacy) still READS it from pre-packs manifests to derive a composition; that is a one-way migration read, not a field to write.
// scope_dial.gates + autonomy — configu: gates is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for which operator review-stops pause the run; a stage's hard stop fires iff its gate token is true. Five tokens: spec (/challenge-prd close — the reviewed spec; /create-prd inherits it only when the operator skips the review), design (/design winner-pick/confirm), build (END-OF-BUILD review at /test close — the operator's single look at the whole implementation via the Components Preview page; fires on content-sdk runs, where the build phase finishes before the post-authoring final gate; INERT on non-content runs, which review the build at the final gate below), final (/test for non-content OR /test-content for content — the last look), go_live (confirm before ANY outward/real-world mutation: /provision-sitecoreai real provisioning, /implement first real-tenant write, /test Components Preview fixture composition (QA 07), /author-content + /test-content live writes, and the /publish go-live). All default true = today's behavior. The build phase is autonomous either way — build/final is the ONLY operator stop during/after the build, never a per-component or mid-build one (rule 71-delivery-loop.mdc).
extra_stops[] holds operator-named ADDITIONAL soft-stage stops promoted to hard (e.g. 'architect', 'task-breakdown', 'provision-sitecoreai', 'implement').

autonomy is a DERIVED human-readable label, not the source of truth: auto_3_gates = all five gates true + no extra_stops (default, no opinion — the '3' is legacy shorthand for the review gates; build joins them on content-sdk runs and is inert elsewhere, so the effective review-stop count per run is still ~3); fully_autonomous = all five gates false + no extra_stops (TRULY ZERO — nothing pauses, live publish + real-tenant boundaries proceed unattended); custom = any other combination. Legacy manifests without the build token treat it as true (default). Legacy manifests with autonomy: extra_stops map to custom with the listed stops.

GENUINE BLOCKERS ARE NOT GATES and always stop regardless of the gate set: a stage that cannot complete (build/publish-job failure), the bug can't-reproduce / not-contained valves, and any [BLOCKER]-tagged Operator Checkpoint item. fully_autonomous removes the REVIEW stops + boundary confirms, not error handling — there is no autonomous path past a hard failure, so it is surfaced.

delivery_loop sets the build-phase TEST-LEG cadence (rule 71-delivery-loop.mdc). CHANGED 2026-07-29: the dial moves the QA leg ONLY — /code-review runs per component tranche under BOTH values (it is diff-local and cheap; batching it saves nearly nothing and lets a defect sit under N tranches of new work, whereas /test is integration-scoped and O(tranches x full-build) is the real cost driver). per_component (DEFAULT, 'standard') = the full {Developer->Code-Reviewer->QA} triad per tranche, looping back to the Developer on a Critical/Major or a test fail before the next component starts (best quality — small diffs, every component proven green; more time + tokens); once = a {Developer->Code-Reviewer} PAIR per tranche (implement -> review its diff -> bounded-3 loop-back -> COMMIT + RECORD at review-clean), then a SINGLE /test over the whole build once every tranche is review-clean, with bounded (3-cycle) whole-build loop-back whose fix diff is code-reviewed as normal (cheaper — one full suite/lint/build instead of N — at the cost of cross-component regressions surfacing late). Converges with delivery_parallelism=parallel, which is review-local + one post-merge QA by construction. INERT on single-tranche runs — a bug / small FRD / freeform run collapses to one implement→review→test pass regardless of this dial. Absent/legacy ⇒ per_component.

content_authoring gates the Content SDK content phase (/discover-components → /author-content ⇄ /test-content → /publish): auto (default) = phase runs iff the active platform pack declares the content_authoring dial; yes = force the content phase; no = skip it entirely (/ship is terminal, the content-phase commands are not recommended).

imagery is the empty-Image-field commissioning tier for /author-content (Sitecore channel), meaningful only when content_authoring runs: gemini (default) = real image generation via solo-sitecore-image-generation (brief → generate → operator review → upload → link → verify); mood = Claude-generated abstract/decorative SVG/gradient/generative-pattern imagery (no external service, no per-image cost) landed via the same skill; none = leave empty Image fields empty (CSS fallback). Absent/legacy ⇒ gemini (the standing 'imagery is a standard authoring step' default).

external_reference governs whether the run may consult PEER PRODUCTS in this repo (velaro/verdure) for reference implementations: prohibited = build only from this product's own code + sanctioned shared knowledge (STOP-and-ask if a sibling would solve a wall); cite-required (default) = reference allowed but every borrowed peer-product pattern is logged (what + from where) + a reliance count reported at /ship; free = no logging. Never restricts the sitecore:* skills, node_modules .d.ts (rule 40), or the shared cm/. See rule 20-boundaries + glossary 'External reference'. Absent/legacy ⇒ cite.

output_verbosity (rule 73-output-verbosity.mdc) controls MID-TURN chat narration, not artifacts on disk: asked at /create-prd Call 3 (Narration). auto (DEFAULT / Recommended) = each agent keeps its frontmatter pin (execution roles minimal, planning roles verbose) UNLESS autonomy is fully_autonomous, which forces minimal on every spawn; minimal = force minimal everywhere (cheapest autonomous runs); verbose = force verbose everywhere (debug / watch a run). Spawn prompts MUST include 'Output Level: <minimal|verbose>'. Slash override: verbosity=auto|minimal|verbose. Absent/legacy ⇒ auto.
// content_policy — guidance (schema 8+): Set at /author-content kickoff for the Sitecore channel (the only channel with placeholders); inherited by /test-content. Absent/null on non-content runs and on legacy manifests — readers treat absence as enforce_placeholder_restrictions: true (follow the rules, the safe default).

enforce_placeholder_restrictions (bool, default true): when true, the Content Author (14) composes ONLY renderings that the Marketer MCP `get_allowed_comps_by_ph(pageId, placeholder)` returns as allowed for the target placeholder — a desired-but-disallowed rendering is substituted with an allowed alternative or surfaced to the operator, never force-placed. When false (operator opted out), the author places renderings by best-fit regardless of the allowed set, but STILL records each placement that falls outside the allowed set as a deviation (so /test-content and the operator can see it).
/test-content structure axis reads this flag: an out-of-allowed-set placement is a MAJOR structure finding under enforce=true, and a recorded (accepted) deviation under enforce=false.
// source — clone scope guidance (schema: clone_scope_mode clarifies delivery intent when source-analysis ran in rebuild mode.
Use home_plus_top5_primary_nav for a bootstrap parity slice; use full_website_clone when the run's definition of done is exact full-clone parity (route + component + content).

When clone_scope_mode is full_website_clone, source-analysis should emit clone_handover_artifact and downstream planning commands (/architect, /task-breakdown) must load source_analysis_artifact + content_dump + assets_bundle + clone_handover_artifact.
Use none when source-analysis did not run or analysis_mode is greenfield.

intake.// note: Set when the run was sourced via /triage (intake-pipeline). /ship reads this to close out the source at ship close (10-ship.md § 15a-intake for local, step 18 for github). Null/absent for runs started directly via /create-prd|frd|bug.
intake.// routed_by: Which command routed this work item here (/triage, /start-flow, or null for a direct /create-*). Was hardcoded to "/triage" until 2026-08-28, so every --init seeded manifest claimed a provenance it did not have.

// canonical_artifacts — schema-7 deltas: implementation_runbook REMOVED in schema 7. The task breakdown's § 0 (Quick orientation) now carries target directory + canonical inputs + delivery order. Reading a schema-6 manifest? Treat any present implementation_runbook entry as legacy/archived; do not produce new ones.

baseline ADDED in schema 7. Optional path to project-planning/baseline.md (architecture baseline) promoted from stable ADRs after the 5-ADR threshold per `/architect` baseline-promotion gate. Null when no baseline has been promoted.
status_index ADDED in schema 7. Path to project-planning/STATUS.md (per-product PRD index). Auto-generated by /create-prd kickoff and /ship close.

stage_history.notes: light rigor, 5 questions, closed on budget. Two push-backs; the second changed the product (Mode A removes external checking).
Recap confirmed without changes, including slug link-health-lens and probing assumption A2 rather than dropping it.
prd-000.md (18 headings) + mechanically extracted prd-minimal-000.md (7 sections) + 3 new ADRs. track=minimal, so ADRs carry the architecture.
The drafted spec was replaced by the reviewed one at /challenge-prd close.

stage_history.one_line: light review; 13 challenges (3 blocker / 6 major / 4 minor); merged into prd-000.md
escalations: G3 — phase 1 needs a named tenant, a settled app_name and operator-guided App Studio registration; nothing in the run supplies them. Operator chose to settle it before /architect, so this close is a hard stop.

// stage_history — schema 7 contract: Schema 7 replaces the prose `notes` essay with structured fields. Required: stage, agent, entered_at, exited_at, outcome, one_line, deliverables. Optional: escalations[] (mirror of operator_attention items raised at this stage), error (on failure), notes (free-form ESCAPE HATCH — keep ≤2 sentences; prefer one_line + escalations).
failed    — stage hit an unrecoverable error; error field populated
skipped   — stage was explicitly bypassed (e.g. user said 'skip discovery')
superseded — a later stage replaced this stage's outputs (e.g. PRD revision after critical review)
partial   — stage completed but with caveats (e.g. some tasks deferred; one_line states what)
`one_line` is the at-a-glance summary /status reads. Keep tight; details belong in deliverables[] and the artifact itself.
`deliverables[]` lists EVERY file the stage wrote or updated by repo-relative path. /status uses this to surface 'what changed at this stage'.

`escalations[]` mirrors operator_attention entries raised AT this stage. The top-level operator_attention[] is still the SoT for cross-product roll-up; this per-stage slice is for forensic queries ('what concerns did /architect raise?').

Backward compatibility: schema-6 manifests have stage_history entries with a freeform `notes` field instead of `one_line` + `deliverables` + `escalations`. Readers should treat schema-6 `notes` as the one_line equivalent and skip the structured fields.
next_action: BLOCKED on operator action: name the tenant, settle app_name, complete Cloud Portal App Studio registration, and name a known-bad + known-good control page. Then /architect.
// next_action — crash-resilience / resu: Written by EVERY stage/tranche/component close (alongside the stage_history entry + git commit — the per-unit checkpoint, rule 71-delivery-loop.mdc / 72-orchestrator-discipline.mdc). States the explicit next step in plain terms so a fresh orchestrator (after a crash/disconnect) knows exactly where to continue WITHOUT re-deriving it from context.
/resume reads this after reconciling disk + git against the manifest (see .agent/commands/project/resume.md): diff reality → update the manifest to match → continue from next_action.

During the per-component delivery loop, next_action names the current component + leg (e.g. 'code-review the Hero tranche' → 'test the Hero tranche' → 'implement the Footer tranche'), so a mid-loop crash resumes the exact triad member.

Backward-compatible: absent on legacy (schema-7-and-prior) manifests and on runs that predate this field — readers treat its absence as 'resume from the last stage_history entry' (the pre-next_action behavior). Never load-bearing for existing runs.
// smoke_outcomes — category guidance: host_frame_smoke: 5-axis pixel comparison vs POC (canonical, see the marketplace-sdk-host-frame-testing skill). Verifies 'did we ship the design'.

live_walkthrough: editor-driven exploration of the installed app on a real tenant for 5+ minutes. Verifies 'does the design actually work for the user'. REQUIRED when the stage brief declares requires_smoke with a host-framed visual_harness, before status can be 'shipped' (vs 'shipped_with_caveats'). Component Usage Atlas's S8/S9/S10/S11 — and S22/S23 — were all live-walkthrough findings that the host-frame smoke could not have caught.
registration: marketplace registration outcome (Cloud Portal app entry + scopes).

operator_attention.item: The tenant-facing app_name is unresolved and Cloud Portal App Studio registration must happen BEFORE /implement — ClientSDK.init() handshakes with the portal and there is no registration API (probe 0a, refuted 2026-08-15). This is operator-guided by construction, so it stops the run regardless of gates.go_live being off.

A2 — path-by-url can distinguish 'page missing' from 'page exists but unpublished'. Unconfirmed, and US-3 (unpublished-target detection) is a headline feature resting on it. AC-3.3 pre-commits a merged 'not found or not published' label so a refutation degrades the feature honestly instead of mislabelling.
A1 — the page-HTML endpoint returns rendered HTML, not layout JSON. If it returns layout, link extraction is different work and tranche 2 is reshaped. Probed in tranche 1.

A3 — chrome links attribute to an owning datasource often enough for best-effort to read as partial rather than blank. Threshold ~50%, measured as M3 at phase 4 exit; below it is a UX re-decision for the operator.

Name/scope tension kept deliberately: the app is called Link Health Lens and never checks the health of an external link. Mitigated in-product (UI is forbidden from saying broken/dead/404/unreachable; metric M5 greps for it at every /code-review) rather than by renaming. Operator confirmed the name at the discovery checkpoint.

PRD-000 is 560 lines against the template's ~400 soft cap. The cap's prescribed remedy is phasing, which § 12a applies; the volume is 8 stories x acceptance criteria + 17 FRs + a self-contained Developer slice. Flagged rather than trimmed, because trimming would have cut acceptance criteria.

gates.spec is off, so /challenge-prd will interrogate and then close SOFT rather than stopping for approval. The spec reaches /architect without a human confirmation step — that is the dial the operator set, recorded here so it is visible rather than inferred.

[BLOCKER] G3 — before /architect: name the tenant, settle app_name, complete Cloud Portal App Studio registration (human Org Admin, no API — probe 0a), and name a known-bad page plus a known-good control page. Phase 1 is blocking and every phase exit is real-tenant-bound; without these the run reaches /implement and stops dead with nobody summoned. Operator chose 'settle it now' over an extra_stops entry.

A4 (new) — the page-HTML endpoint exposes a structural signal sufficient to separate chrome from page content. The entire three-way label rests on it and nobody has seen it. T0 probe (f) is blocking; a refutation is an operator re-decision (R8), NOT an implementation fallback — reverting to attribution-derived origin would reinstate the unfailable M3 that ADR-0006 exists to prevent.

The spec grew 561 -> 658 lines against the ~400 soft cap. The PM removed every duplication it introduced; the residue is requirement text the review obliged (6 new ACs, 2 new FRs, the status-set model, A4, R8, two probe questions, the phase preconditions). Further cuts would remove decisions, not padding. Operator call whether to trim.

G1 and G2 were both blockers caused by the SAME thing: the mid-discovery reframe from broken-link checking to internal-link integrity was complete in the narrative sections and incomplete in the requirements layer. A spec can read as fully reframed in section 1 and still instruct an implementer to build the old product in section 7.

// operator_attention — guidance: Mirrors the Operator Checkpoint block (see .agent/glossary.md § Operator Checkpoint) so /status can roll up unresolved attention items across products.
Append-only: never edit a prior entry in place. To mark an item resolved, append a new entry with kind: 'resolved' and references: <prior raised_at>.
Severity guidance: 'blocker' means the next stage cannot proceed; 'warn' means the run can continue but the operator should know; 'info' is FYI.

Kind values map 1:1 to the Operator Checkpoint sections: decision → Decisions needed, assumption → Assumptions made, concern → Concerns / risks, question → Open questions, resolved → resolution of a prior entry.

// guidance: RETIRED (schema 8+). Both archive triggers are gone: supersession archiving (moved a superseded task-breakdown / ui-design / architecture into archive/ at the next stage write) and the post-ship scaffolding sweep (/ship step 15b). Neither moves anything now, and notes.archive_skip is retired with them.

Replaced by ARTIFACT DURABILITY TIERING, enforced declaratively by project-planning/.gitignore (seeded at /create-prd step 4a from .agent/templates/project-planning-seed/.gitignore). Same intent, no file movement.

TIER 1 — TRACKED (the durable record): spec (prd/frd/bug-NNN.md), ADR/, baseline.md, plans/ship-report-*.md, plans/*probe-findings*.md, captures/, spike-notes/, smoke/, source-analysis/, STATUS.md, tasks.md, workflow/run-<id>.json.

TIERS 2-4 — UNTRACKED (produced and read by the pipeline exactly as before, never committed): *-minimal-NNN.md (compiler output); task-breakdown / qa-report / code-review / test-report, architecture/, brain-dumps/, ui-design/, design-prototypes/ (run-scoped working material); workflow/current-run.json (mutable machine state — byte-identical to the latest run-<id>.json, which IS tracked).
canonical_artifacts.* paths are therefore STABLE — no stage rewrites them to an archive location, so a later /document or design-polish run resolves the same path the producing stage wrote.

Legacy products may still have an archive/ folder holding durable artifacts the retired sweep trapped there (probe findings, smoke notes, even ship reports). /ship § 15b-promote rescues those back to plans/ before the folder is untracked. See .agent/manifests/README.md § 'Artifact durability tiers'.

// notes: OBJECT, not an array. 17 contract citations address it as notes.<key> — base_branch, program, sdk_surface_split, split_override, critical_review, scope_dial, composition_detected_from and more. The template declared an ARRAY, which produced real manifests of both shapes in the same workspace. Corrected 2026-08-24 after a throwaway run had to pass --replace notes to write a documented key.

notes.grill_relay: The grill ran inline via orchestrator relay rather than inside the spawned PM: an interactive multi-turn interrogation cannot interleave with the operator from a background subagent. The constructive spawn received the ledger PATH only (rule 72).
notes.product_reframe: Discovery Q4/Q5 changed the product. variables.mode = client-side removes every outbound network check, so broken-link / redirect-chain / DNS detection is PERMANENTLY out of scope and the spec is internal-link integrity. See ADR-0002.
notes.critical_review_gaps: 13 total — 3 blocker, 6 major, 4 minor. Triage: 4 operator-decision (grilled), 8 self-resolvable (fixed without asking), 1 verifiable (routed to the T0 probe as question (e)).

// discovery_mode: How the grill actually reached a human, if it did. `unattended` MUST carry discovery_questions_asked: 0 — a non-zero count there means answers were invented, which the interrogation protocol prohibits absolutely. Added 2026-08-26 after six runs each improvised their own free-text note because no field existed, and a fabricated ledger was indistinguishable from a real one on the manifest.
// source.portability_caveats: NULL, never []. `method:clone` states: "An empty caveat list is a CLAIM, not a default. On a real clone, empty is evidence the check did not run." The template shipped `[]` for one day (2026-08-27), so --init wrote the exact value the owning pack forbids and a run that left it would have read as "we checked and found none" while having asked nobody.
